user.description:
Spook floats around your Home Assistant looking for ghosts: references to things that no longer exist, and leftovers nobody cleaned up. Whatever it finds, it reports under Repairs.

It also extends what your automations and scripts can do, with extra actions, triggers, conditions and helpers, for even more powerful automations.

Fair warning: Spook is not part of Home Assistant. It is a custom integration that reaches into places it was never invited. If something odd happens, suspect Spook first, and [let us know]({issue_tracker_url}).

Ready to get spooked?

init.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your energy dashboard 👻

The energy dashboard references the following entities, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{entities}

This usually happens when an entity used in the energy configuration was renamed or removed. Renamed? Then open [Settings > Dashboards > Energy](/config/energy) and pick the new one, so its history stays on the dashboard.

Removed for good? Spook can take these out of the energy configuration for you. A missing meter takes its source or device along, a missing price or cost is only cleared. The dashboard then stops showing the history of what is taken out; the statistics themselves stay.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

Spook has found a ghost in your notify groups 👻

The notify group `{group}` forwards to the following actions, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{members}

The group still delivers to the rest of its members, and it still reports success to whatever called it, so nothing upstream notices. The failure surfaces only as a stray "Task exception was never retrieved" in the log, which names no group and reads like a bug. Whoever was behind that member simply stops being notified.

To fix this error, edit the `services:` list of this group in your configuration and remove or correct these entries.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

Spook has found a ghost in your dashboards 👻

This dashboard resource is listed {count} times:

{resources}

This usually happens when a custom card was updated by adding a resource for the new version instead of editing the one already there. The browser loads both, the card tries to register itself twice, and the second attempt fails, which looks like a broken card rather than a duplicated resource.

Spook can clear the extra copies and keep the most recently added one.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

menu_options.remove: Clear the extra copies, keep the most recent

abort.issue_ignored: Spook will keep quiet about this resource from now on.
abort.manage: You can manage your dashboard resources yourself on the [Resources page](/config/lovelace/resources).
abort.yaml: These resources are listed in your YAML configuration, so Spook cannot change them for you. Edit the `resources:` section of your Lovelace configuration and remove the copies of `{resource}` you no longer need.

lovelace_unknown_service_references.title: Unknown actions used in dashboard: {dashboard}
lovelace_unknown_service_references.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your dashboards 👻

While floating around, Spook crossed path with the following dashboard:

[{dashboard}]({edit})

This dashboard performs the following actions, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{services}



A button or card using one of these does nothing when tapped. This often happens when a script was renamed or removed, or an integration was removed. To fix this error, [edit the dashboard]({edit}) and remove or replace these non-existing actions.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

homekit_unknown_entity_references.title: Unknown entities used in HomeKit bridge: {bridge}
homekit_unknown_entity_references.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your HomeKit bridge 👻

While floating around, Spook crossed path with the following HomeKit bridge:

{bridge}

This bridge names the following entities, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{entities}



HomeKit does not follow an entity that is renamed. An included entity that was renamed or removed is gone from the Home app; an excluded entity that was renamed shows up in it again.

To fix this error, go to [the HomeKit Bridge integration](/config/integrations/integration/homekit), select **Configure** on this bridge, and pick the entities again.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

homekit_unknown_entity_references_yaml.title: Unknown entities used in HomeKit bridge: {bridge}
homekit_unknown_entity_references_yaml.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your HomeKit bridge 👻

While floating around, Spook crossed path with the following HomeKit bridge:

{bridge}

This bridge names the following entities, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{entities}



HomeKit does not follow an entity that is renamed. An included entity that was renamed or removed is gone from the Home app; an excluded entity that was renamed shows up in it again.

This bridge is set up in your YAML configuration. To fix this error, edit the `filter` of this bridge under `homekit:` and remove or correct these entities.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

triggered_by_user.name: Triggered by a user

A schedule, the sun, or an integration acting on its own carries nobody, and neither does forcing a run with the Run button.

target_temperature_reached.description: Fires when the temperature of a thermostat or water heater reaches its target, or jumps past it. Changing the target does not count, and neither does a device that is off.

tolerance.name: Tolerance
tolerance.description: How close to the target still counts as there, in the device's unit. For a thermostat that settles just short of its setpoint. Zero means the target itself.

update_installed.name: Update installed
update_installed.description: Fires when an update entity reports a different installed version, whether somebody pressed install, the device updated itself, or it was updated outside of Home Assistant.

position_reached.name: Position reached
position_reached.description: Fires when a cover or valve gets to a position, or moves past it. One that is already there, or comes back from unavailable at it, does not count.

position.name: Position
position.description: The position to reach, from 0 (closed) to 100 (open).

script_started.name: Script started
script_started.description: Fires when a script starts a run. A run the script refuses, because it is already running, does not count. Leave the target empty to watch every script.

debounce.name: Once it settles
debounce.description: Fires once a trigger has stopped firing for a while, so a burst of them arrives as one. A motion sensor does not report motion once, it reports it twenty times.

triggers.name: Triggers
triggers.description: The triggers to wait out. Any of them firing starts a burst and any of them firing again keeps it going, so several triggers are collapsed together rather than one at a time.

for.name: For
for.description: How long it has to have been quiet before this fires. Every firing starts that wait over, so something that never stops firing never gets reported.

all_of.name: All of these happened
all_of.description: Fires when every one of several triggers has fired inside the same window of time, in any order. Home Assistant's own triggers are a list where any one of them is enough; this is the other one.

triggers.name: Triggers
triggers.description: The triggers that all have to have fired. Order does not matter, and a trigger firing again replaces its earlier turn rather than counting twice.

within.name: Within
within.description: How close together they have to be. The window slides, so a trigger that fired longer ago than this is forgotten while the others carry on counting.

recovered.name: Entity came back
recovered.description: Fires when an entity comes back after having been unavailable for a while, so a router rebooting does not read as everything in the house recovering.

for.name: For
for.description: How long the entity has to have been away before coming back counts. Anything shorter is a flicker: reloading an integration takes every one of its entities through unavailable and back inside a second.

user_added.name: User added
user_added.description: Fires when somebody is given a login to Home Assistant. Users Home Assistant creates for its own integrations are left out.

integration_added.name: Integration added
integration_added.description: Fires when an integration is added to Home Assistant, whoever or whatever added it.

device_added.name: Device added
device_added.description: Fires when a new device is added to Home Assistant, like a plug that was just paired.

device_discovered.name: Device discovered
device_discovered.description: Fires when Home Assistant discovers something new it could set up, like a device that just turned up on your network.
